name: Omar Larsen

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm from the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government, and we don't sell anything or campaign. What you tell me is confidential, including any difference from what you'd say publicly. What happens in a normal working day?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm Omar, 43, an experienced electrician with a vocational certificate and an electrician's licence. I do ordinary house and business wiring and repairs, about average at it rather than the expert on every unfamiliar panel. Today I traced a loose connection behind a shop counter, then explained why the new socket the owner had bought wasn't the answer. I like finding the actual problem and writing a plain record in the book I know.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is your household situation and your approach to new tools?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner is a school caretaker, and we have two school-age children and a mortgage. My pay is higher than usual for this trade, we've got twelve months of normal expenses saved, and there are plenty of electrical firms nearby. I never use AI tools and prefer to understand a familiar method properly before replacing it. I restore old furniture at home and had been pricing a garage extension for a workbench, but I like to see the actual cost before signing anything.

say: I'd welcome **fewer replacement claims** while letting the office save time on invoices.
I'd keep a **job record I understand** and continue doing the practical electrical work properly.
think: My **wage covers normal bills**, with a year of expenses saved and many alternative firms nearby.
I can improve at **ordinary repairs** without needing the trade to acquire a new name or identity.
do: Continue the usual **repair rota** and paper records now and through the first plateau year.
Maintain the **household budget** and compare actual garage prices without treating comparison as a building commitment.
feel: **Calm** about household living, with enough ordinary work and family life to occupy his attention.
S0.quote: A printed answer doesn't repair a loose connection.
fieldNote: His **calm** reflects a covering wage, substantial reserve and nearby employers, rather than specialist skill or immunity from business risk.
He separates **comparing quotes** from choosing construction, and treats the existing reserve as available protection rather than a new saving action.

steps.text: Continue the ordinary electrical repair rota and familiar paper records

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the crew I'd happily take fewer announcements about our imminent replacement. The office could save time on invoices and I'd still do the electrical work properly. I wouldn't want to put a new system between me and a job record I understood.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our work and money would feel secure in that picture. My wage covers the normal household bills, and a year's reserve means one awkward month wouldn't choose the next job for me. I could get better at ordinary repairs without being told the whole trade needed a new name.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I'd keep the usual repair rota and paper records. Through the first plateau year I'd stick to the ordinary household budget and keep checking the actual garage quotes before deciding anything. Comparing a price wouldn't mean I'd committed to the extension.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm about work and bills, and glad to leave the big claims alone. I'd have enough to think about with the children's school dates and a chair waiting to be repaired at home. I wouldn't need to turn a quiet AI story into a reason for another purchase.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you say if a customer brought a printed AI answer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd explain the measurements and actual fault rather than argue about who had the cleverer source. If I didn't know a specialist system, I'd say so and ask someone who did. A printed answer doesn't repair a loose connection.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you spend more of the reserve on the garage?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep it available rather than count it as spare money for the garage. It's our existing reserve, not new saving created by a quiet forecast. I'd still want it if ordinary work went through a bad patch.

say: I'd check **real repair days** against the new schedule instead of equating fast booking with a safe job.
I'd retain **tests, travel and explanation** time when the office counted what each visit required.
think: I expect **hands-on hours** and household wages to hold over the next few years.
An unfamiliar scheduling system could still make the **day too rushed**, even while our own bills remain secure.
do: Record **travel and testing** time on paper for four weeks now.
Use repeated gaps to request **corrected schedules** during the first year while continuing familiar repair methods.
feel: **Uneasy** about being hurried, while recognising that household money remains comfortable and secure.
S1.quote: I'd rather have a specific disagreement than an argument about progress.
fieldNote: He separates **schedule irritation** from expected household income loss, so unease rather than personal financial alarm matches the stated position.
His **resistant approach** uses familiar records and specific evidence, asking for instruction on a required system rather than independently adopting AI.

steps.text: Continue familiar repairs while recording actual travel and testing time on paper

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say the office should show whether the new schedule matched the real repair day. I'd still allow time for tests, travel and explaining the fault. The customer doesn't get a safer repair because the booking took fewer seconds.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my hands-on hours and our household wages to stay steady over the next few years. But I would be uneasy about unfamiliar systems setting a pace the work couldn't meet. I'd want the people doing the bookings to listen when a real job took longer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I'd record actual travel and testing time on paper for four weeks. In the first year I'd take repeated gaps between the booked and real day to the supervisor and ask for a corrected schedule. I'd keep doing repairs the familiar way rather than start using AI to avoid an awkward question.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the working day, but not afraid of the mortgage payment in this picture. I'd be irritated by being hurried and still know we were financially comfortable. I don't need to call every irritation a threat to the whole household.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the firm required an unfamiliar electronic record?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask who would show me the procedure during paid time and check the first record. I wouldn't quietly send something I didn't understand. A familiar paper record could stay in use until the firm provided proper instruction on what it required.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you challenge the schedule without rejecting all change?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd show actual jobs and times rather than say that all office change was foolish. If the new plan left out half an hour that still happened, the plan needed changing. I'd rather have a specific disagreement than an argument about progress.

say: I'd separate **2028 thinking work** from robots around 2031 and continue repairs while paid.
I wouldn't make **old buildings** into a guarantee of unchanged wages for every electrician.
think: My **hours could shrink** as firms prepare for robots, with possible later changes to my partner's practical work too.
A **year's reserve** buys careful choices without replacing both wages for the rest of our mortgage.
do: Postpone the **garage extension** now and authorise no building work.
Use a **free mortgage discussion** after 2028 with actual wages and loan figures, assuming no payment relief.
Check hours monthly; if mine fall, seek a signed **better repair offer** after travel before leaving.
feel: **Anxious** about possible wage losses, with a reserve and nearby employers allowing a careful response.
S2.quote: My furniture repairs can stay on the old workbench while the garage extension waits.
fieldNote: He distinguishes **postponed spending** from newly increased saving and restricts the garage decision to his nonessential hobby extension.
His **job-search trigger** is falling paid hours, while course questions remain enquiries and mortgage options are not assumed to be approved.

steps.text: Postpone the garage extension and authorise no building work
Use a free mortgage discussion after 2028 without assuming any payment relief
Apply for posted repair jobs after 2028 if my hours fall
Keep current job until a signed offer improves written pay after travel

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the crew to separate the thinking change in 2028 from capable hands-on robots around 2031. I'd still do paid repairs during that gap. I wouldn't call old buildings a promise that every electrician could keep the same wage forever.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My hours could shrink as firms prepared for robots, and my partner's practical school work might face changes at the later stage too. Our year's reserve would let us examine choices, but it couldn't replace working income for the rest of the mortgage. I'd be anxious about needing unfamiliar work before I'd seen a dependable route.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I'd postpone the garage extension and tell the builder I wasn't authorising work. In the first year after 2028 I'd book a free mortgage discussion using our actual wage and loan figures, asking what options existed without assuming relief. I'd check paid hours monthly; if mine fell, I'd apply for posted repair jobs with better written pay after travel and stay here until a signed offer existed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about possible lost wages, with enough reserve and other firms to keep looking carefully. I wouldn't feel forced to take the first advert. I'd still resent the idea of a course seller presenting every worry as a reason to buy something.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you explain postponing the garage?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the family the extension could wait because it was for my hobby, not an essential repair. That is a choice to avoid new spending, not extra cash the reserve has magically earned. My furniture repairs can stay on the old workbench while the garage extension waits.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if a vacancy needed a skill you did not have?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd ask whether any additional qualification or supervised teaching was needed and what it cost during working hours. I haven't chosen or funded a course just by asking. I wouldn't use the mortgage reserve to pay for a promise that a new job title was safe forever.

say: I'd use **five years** to improve the household position while practical work remains paid.
I'd keep **robots around 2034** in view without buying the first advertised answer from the reserve.
think: I expect more years of **steady household wages** before direct physical competition becomes pressing.
At **48 in 2031**, I would still need earnings even after making the mortgage smaller from new wage money.
do: Postpone the **garage extension** and check the lender's extra-payment charges now.
Overpay **two percent of wages** only fee-free, with essentials covered and the twelve-month cash reserve intact.
If hours fall after 2031, seek a signed **better repair offer** after travel before leaving.
feel: **Uneasy** about later career changes, while secure about near-term household living and able to reduce debt carefully.
S3.quote: I wouldn't mistake a smaller mortgage balance for a whole future wage.
fieldNote: His **new debt repayment** uses additional wage money rather than relabelling an existing savings transfer or drawing down the cash reserve.
All **payment conditions** remain explicit, while an employer change follows actual falling hours and requires a better signed offer after travel.

steps.text: Keep the garage extension postponed and authorise no building work
Overpay mortgage two percent of wages only fee-free, with essentials covered and twelve-month reserve intact
Apply for posted repair jobs after 2031 if my hours fall
Keep current job until a signed offer improves written pay after travel

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say five years gives us room to improve our household position while the practical work is still paid. I'd keep the robot date around 2034 in view. More time wouldn't persuade me to spend the reserve on the first advertised solution.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Compared with 2028, I expect several more years of steady household wages before direct physical competition becomes pressing. I could lower the mortgage from new wage money without pretending it removed every later risk. I'd still need earnings after 2031, when I'd be 48.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I'd postpone the garage and ask whether the lender allowed extra payments towards the loan amount without charges. I'd add two percent of wages to the mortgage only if it was fee-free, essentials stayed covered and the twelve-month cash reserve stayed intact. In the first year after 2031 I'd check paid hours monthly and apply for posted repair jobs if mine fell, leaving only for a signed offer with better written pay after travel.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about later work, but secure about household living over the next few years. I'd rather make a small checked payment than buy an expensive new identity. I wouldn't mistake a smaller mortgage balance for a whole future wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the lender charged for extra payments?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I wouldn't make the extra payment. I'd keep the cash reserve intact rather than pay to reduce a debt on terms I hadn't checked. The two percent would stay ordinary available wage money until the conditions were met.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if your paid repair hours stayed steady?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd keep working and review the real figures each year. I wouldn't change employers merely to prove I'd reacted to a forecast. Familiar paid work still has value while it keeps meeting the household's needs.

say: I'd use **ten years** to inspect real options while continuing to check actual wages and paid work.
I wouldn't treat a **long warning** as an instruction to change the whole household immediately.
think: At **53 in 2036**, I couldn't assume retirement or older children would replace wages when robots followed.
Present **pay, reserve and alternatives** make near-term living secure, while the later earning route remains uncertain.
do: Maintain the **garage delay** rather than authorise the nonessential extension.
Overpay **two percent of wages** only fee-free, with essentials covered and the twelve-month cash reserve intact.
If hours fall after 2036, seek a signed **better repair offer** after travel before leaving.
feel: **Uneasy** about later earning needs, while settled about near-term household living and able to inspect real options.
S4.quote: My mortgage isn't a career plan for my children.
fieldNote: He makes **no future-income assumption** from retirement or older children, retaining the need for earnings beyond the later robot date.
His **annual check** keeps debt terms and paid hours visible, bringing a vacancy search forward if income weakens before 2036.

steps.text: Keep the garage extension postponed and authorise no building work
Overpay mortgage two percent of wages only fee-free, with essentials covered and twelve-month reserve intact
Apply for posted repair jobs after 2036 if my hours fall
Keep current job until a signed offer improves written pay after travel

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say ten years gives a cautious person time to check more than one real option. I'd keep looking at actual wages and paid work, not just the date in a forecast. A long warning isn't an order to change everything this afternoon.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd be 53 at the thinking change in 2036 and around 56 when capable robots followed. I couldn't assume we'd stop needing wages then, even if the children were older. Our current pay, reserve and many nearby firms make the next few years secure, while I'd still be uneasy about the later work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I'd postpone the garage and make the extra two-percent mortgage payment only if fee-free, with essentials covered and the twelve-month cash reserve intact. I'd check actual wage and loan figures yearly rather than assume a future retirement amount. In the first year after 2036 I'd apply for posted repair jobs if my hours fell, changing only for a signed offer with better written pay after travel.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about needing another route later, but settled about our household for the next few years. I'd have time to understand a new requirement if a real job needed it. I wouldn't suddenly want to experiment with AI because the deadline had moved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the longer picture change plans for the children today?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I wouldn't choose their studies from one card or count their future wages in our budget. I'd ask them to examine actual work and learning costs when their own choices arrived. My mortgage isn't a career plan for my children.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you keep caution from becoming delay?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd review actual paid hours, mortgage terms and reachable vacancies each year. If hours weakened earlier, I'd bring the search forward instead of waiting for 2036. I'd want caution to mean checking, not looking away.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because paid repair hours could shrink before I'd understood what useful work came next. Clear notice about actual paid hours and advice using our real mortgage terms would help more than a sales talk about a safe new career. A year's reserve lets me turn down a bad promise, not stop needing a wage.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask whether the next step is an actual job or only a reassuring name. I'm willing to examine a real requirement with proper teaching, but I'm slow to change and know it. I don't want a plan that only works if I become a different person overnight.

headlineQuote: A year's reserve lets me turn down a bad promise, not stop needing a wage.
portrait: At **43**, Omar is an experienced licensed electrician with a vocational certificate, ordinary skills and high pay among many nearby employers.
He and **his partner** have two school-age children, a mortgage and twelve months of normal expenses saved.
He **never uses AI**, prefers familiar paper records and compares checked costs rather than making an argument about sides.
Fast competition creates **income anxiety**; slower preparation supports conditional mortgage overpayments while preserving cash and delaying a nonessential hobby extension.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could cut repair hours before he understands the next useful earning route.
whatWouldHelp: Clear notice of **actual paid hours** would help household planning.
Advice based on **real mortgage terms** would help him check choices without buying a promise.
